newsitem.title: GERMANY: Listless German shares end pre-Xmas bourse lower.
newsitem.headline: Listless German shares end pre-Xmas bourse lower.

text.p: German shares limped their way to a lower close in thinly traded floor dealings on Monday -- the last day before a three-day Christmas break.
The 30-share DAX index dropped 8.88 points to end at 2,845.57, after hovering in a range of just seven points.

Dealers said the move did not reflect any real weakness in the stock market -- the closing DAX level actually marked a marginal gain from the close of late electronic dealings on Friday. Moreover, volumes were abysmally low.
"At least we've got Solitaire here," said a trader on the Frankfurt bourse. "There is absolutely nothing else to do."
"We should have given ourselves today off as a Christmas present," said a Duesseldorf dealer.
The futures market was somewhat more active, with the March DTB DAX future up 11.5 points at 2,864.5. The December contract expired last week.
Early movers on the cash market included Commerzbank AG, which was down 40 pfennigs at 38.80. The stock has been pushed up in the past few weeks on renewed takeover speculation.
Daimler-Benz drifted down 15 pfennigs to 102.60 amid talk that Mercedes chief Werner Helmut Werner would quit the company, refreshed by the German press at the weekend.
"Werner is a real emblem and if he really leaves then that will be negative for the share," one dealer said.
The outlook for Friday's trade was for similarly thin volumes. The earliest chance of some real activity, one dealer said, was next Monday, the last trading day of 1996.
